questions.q: What does the summary say happens when you try to work faster?
a: Any time you save gets filled with more tasks
Your workday reliably gets shorter
Your focus improves over time
Only new employees struggle with it
questions.why: The first lesson calls speed alone a trap: extra time just gets absorbed by an already full schedule.

questions.q: What did Jack Nevison's research find about long working hours?
a: People working over 55 hours are less productive than those under 50
Productivity rises steadily with every extra hour worked
Overtime only helps on creative projects
Everyone produces the most at around 40 hours
questions.why: The first lesson uses Nevison's review of studies to show that overtime backfires.

questions.q: What does Hyatt say about time and energy?
a: Neither is infinite, so rest has to be planned
Both stay constant throughout the working day
Energy refills on its own every morning
Time can be stretched with better tools
questions.why: The second lesson compares the brain to a phone battery and says both resources run down.

questions.q: Which recovery habit does the summary call the first principle?
a: Sleep
Exercise
Meditation
Socializing
questions.why: The second lesson says sleep comes first because without it problem-solving and decisions suffer.

questions.q: Which question helps you see the hidden cost of agreeing to a request?
a: If I say yes to this, what am I saying no to?
How quickly could I finish this task?
Who else on the team could do this?
Will this make me look dependable?
questions.why: The third lesson borrows this question to expose the trade-off hiding inside every yes.
